questionText:
Considering LiBH$_{4}$ reduces an ester group to the corresponding alcohol and does not reduce a carboxylic acid group, the correct statement about the major products **P, Q, R and S** is:
[Diagram]
solution:
[Diagram]

[Diagram]

**Understanding the role of LiBH$_{4}$**
LiBH$_{4}$ is a reducing agent. It converts **esters** into **alcohols**, but it does not reduce the **carboxylic acid group**. This selectivity helps in predicting which groups will change during the reaction and which will remain the same.
**Forming the products**
In the reaction, only the ester group gets reduced. The carboxylic acid group stays unchanged. Based on this, different compounds form as products, which are labelled as **P, Q, R,** and **S**.
**Relationship between products**
The pairs **P and Q** have the same connectivity but differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms. Similarly, **R and S** also differ in spatial arrangement. These are examples of **diastereomers**, which are a type of stereoisomer that are not mirror images of each other.
**Type of isomerism**
Since the difference arises due to the geometry around the double bond or restricted rotation, **P and Q** as well as **R and S** are specifically **geometrical isomers**, which are a form of diastereomers.
Therefore, **P and Q are diastereomers** and **R and S are diastereomers** because they are **geometrical isomers**.
options: **P & Q** are identical, and **R & S** are diastereomers.
**P & Q** are diastereomers, and **R & S** are identical.
**P & Q** are diastereomers, and **R & S** are diastereomers.
**P & Q** are identical, and **R & S** are identical.

The correct order of acid strength of the following carboxylic acids is

Acidic nature depends upon nature of electron withdrawing group and electronegativity. Electronegativity further depends on % of s character. Higher the s-character, greater will be the electronegativity and hence tendency to loose H increases thus acidic character also increases.


[Diagram]


sp- hybridisation (50% s character) (pK$_{a}$ = 1.86)

II is more acidic than III since electron donating group ($$ - OC{H_3}$$) is attached to benzene ring in III which decreases the acidic character.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questionText:
**Statement 1 :** p-Hydroxybenzoic acid has a lower boiling point than o-hydroxybenzoic acid.
**Statement 2 :** o-Hydroxybenzoic acid has intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
solution:
We know that hydrogen are of two types :
1. Intermolecular hydrogen bonding
2. Intramolecular hydrogen bonding
In any organic compound, if there is ortho substituent and hydrogen bonding is possible in that compound then always the bonding will be intramolecular hydrogen bonding. If the substituent is at para position, then intermolecular hydrogen bonding exists. Therefore, we can say that o-Hydroxybenzoic acid will show intramolecular benzoic acid and p-hydroxybenzoic acid will show intermolecular hydrogen bonding.

[Diagram]

The strength of intermolecular hydrogen bonding is more than intramolecular hydrogen bonding. Therefore we can say that p-hydroxybenzoic acid because of intermolecular hydrogen bonding has a higher boiling point than o-hydroxybenzoic acid. Therefore, statement 1 is false but statement 2 is correct.
Now, if we look at the reason it states that o-hydroxybenzoic acid has intramolecular hydrogen bonding. From the above explanation we can say that this statement is true.
options: Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True, Statement 2 is a CORRECT explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is True, Statement 2 is NOT a CORRECT explanation for Statement 1
Statement 1 is True, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is True
